citations.text: The scanned 本 headword describes the graph as 指事. It says Western Zhou forms add a dot at the part of 木 representing the tree root, and Warring States forms change the dot to a short horizontal stroke. It describes the Shuowen ancient form as 木 above three root-like marks; some Warring States variants use 白 to represent a tree pit. It gives the original meaning as tree root, quotes 《国语·晋语一》 “伐木不自其本，必复生,” and records further uses for plant stem/trunk and figurative fundamental or important matters, including contrast with 末 and an agriculture sense. This is one source’s account; the early graph sequence and the cited works’ composition dates are not independently established here.

citations.text: In its account of the graph sequence under 本, 字源 describes the Shuowen ancient form as 木 above three root-like marks. It separately says that some Warring States forms use 白 to depict a tree pit. These are two distinct proposals in this book’s account; the passage does not establish a sequence between them. The uncommon marks in the Shuowen ancient-form sample are left unidentified.
